newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures posted a new contract high for the second day running as hopes for interest rate cuts in Europe boosted debt markets, overshadowing some disappointment the Bank of France failed to trim rates.

The March bond future rallied to a high of 130.86 after a Bundesbank council member said monetary policy could not be indifferent to the grave unemployment situation in Germany, especially when inflation was not currently a concern.
Traders said the comments, coming on the same day a Bundesbank report said inflation was expected to stay below two percent for two years, were a driving force behind the gains.

Hopes that lower German rates would allow the Bank of France to trim its intervention rate mitigated the negative impact of the fact the central bank left rates on hold after the first meeting of its new policy council, analysts said.

Economists said the Frrench central bank had probably remained cautious to quash speculation the two new members would instigate a looser approach to monetary policy, seen as potentially destabilising for the French franc.
The central bank would continue to ease rates in the weeks and months to come, eventually bring French short-term rates into line with German rates, the economists said.

"Sometime in the next two weeks...assuming the franc holds its current level, we could see at least a small gesture on (the overnight rate)," Patrick Mange, economist at Deutsche Bank in Paris said. "The Bank of France's objective remains to bring French rates down to the level of German rates."

The franc was trading little changed on Thursday around 3.3750 per mark, slightly below 3.35, its central parity against the mark in the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) -- a level meant to reflect economic fundamentals in France and Germany.
March interest rate futures slipped back slightly from a record high of 96.83 after the Bank of France left rates unchanged, but every other PIBOR futures contract posted gains.
The spread between March PIBOR and German Euromark contracts widened however to 13 basis points from 11 on Wednesday. The gap between the June contracts also widened to seven basis points.
Traders said although the March bond future retreated from its new contract high as U.S. bonds declined on stronger than expected economic data, the all-time high of 131.38 was now within sight.

The strong performance of long-dated bonds led to a flattening of the yield curve. The gap between benchmark two- and 10-year French bonds contracted to 225 basis points from 229 basis points on Wednesday.
The spread between French and German benchmark 10-year yields remained stable at minus 15 basis points.

The French Treasury kept up a brisk pace of issuance, required to meet its 1997 funding target of 600 billion francs, selling 22.8 billion francs of BTANs at auction on Thursday with an overall bid-to-cover ratio of 1.8 percent.
